 Nxled sweeps Akari to clinch first semis berth, sets sights on Top 2
 Nxled put its corporate alliance with Akari on the back burner and focused on a far more pressing mission – becoming the first team to punch its ticket to the semifinal round of the Premier Volleyball League All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series.
 The Chameleons delivered in emphatic fashion, turning back the Chargers, 27-25, 25-22, 26-24, at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Thursday to stretch their unbeaten run to six games and officially secure the first Final Four berth, leaving six other teams to battle for the remaining three semis slots.
 More than just another straight-sets victory, the triumph showcased Nxled's offensive firepower, defensive resilience and, perhaps most importantly, its composure and sheer determination when the pressure was at its highest.
 The Chameleons stared at a possible opening-set setback after falling behind, 21-24, but refused to buckle, unleashing a stirring comeback to wrest the frame from the Chargers. They displayed the same steely resolve in the next two sets, holding off a pair of Akari rallies to complete the sweep and move into the post-elimination round ahead of everybody else. 
 The victory, however, came at a physical cost, with Nxled and Akari sustaining injury scares in the third set. 
 Jonah Escamillan hurt her left knee while going for an attack midway through the frame, while Ivy Lacsina hit the back of her head against an LED board as she chased a strong dig from Shiela Pineda late in the set. Both incidents briefly cast a shadow over an otherwise memorable night for the Chameleons. 
 Escamillan's injury came with Nxled trailing, 14-16, but the Chameleons responded by rallying around their teammate, unleashing a 6-2 run to seize a 20-18 lead. 
 Akari, however, refused to go back down. Desperate for a victory to bolster their own semis bid, the Chargers countered with consecutive hits to set up a nerve-racking finish. 
 Setter Mars Alba repeatedly turned to Fifi Sharma for quick attacks, with the combination producing three points, including one that gave Akari a 23-22 advantage. 
 But Nxled remained unshaken. 
 Gel Cayuna came up with a crucial block on Eli Soyud after a brief exchange, while Pineda delivered an unlikely point off a dig from a thunderous Akari attack that sailed over the net and bounced off Zone 1, forcing Lacsina into a desperate chase that ended with her colliding with the LED board. 
 Alba and Sharma connected on another quick play to save a match point, but Cayuna answered with a clever 1-2 play that caught Akari's defense off guard for a 25-24 Nxled lead. 
 After surviving a couple more tense exchanges, Cayuna then set up EJ Cariño for the finishing blow, whose powerful attack caromed off Faith Nisperos' arms and out of bounds to seal the one-hour, 39-minute victory. 
 "We just stuck it out together. Akari is a very hard team for us to play. They're very good in defense and blocking and a very scrappy team, so we communicated early and just had to stay resilient and very patient as the game went on," said Brooke Van Sickle. 
 "I'm very proud that we stuck to it and didn't care about what the score was," she added. 
 Van Sickle once again spearheaded Nxled's attack, delivering 10 points to claim Best Player of the Game honors. 
 Beyond her usual offensive contributions, the Fil-American standout also showcased an increasingly effective left-handed attack, an added weapon she developed out of necessity following a right shoulder injury. 
 Van Sickle said she turned to her left hand to stay involved in training while recovering from the shoulder setback, spending countless hours hitting balls against a wall until the stroke became a more natural part of her game. 
 "After my shoulder injury, being able to participate in training meant using my left so I could still join practice. So it was a lot of time hitting balls against the wall with my left. I just love to play so much that I don't want to separate myself from it," she said. 
 The adjustment has since given Van Sickle another dimension to her attack – and Nxled another weapon as it heads into the semifinals with its winning momentum intact. 
 MJ Phillips, Myla Pablo and Cariño chipped in nine points apiece, while Jackie Acuña and Escamillan added six each, allowing Nxled to match Akari’s 48-attack output. 
 The Chameleons, however, held the advantage at the net, outblocking the Chargers, 12-7 with Pablo and Phillips contributed four and three, respectively. 
 Eli Soyud continued to spearhead Akari’s offense with 16 points, while Ced Domingo provided support with 10. Sharma, Nisperos and Lacsina chipped in six points apiece for the Chargers, who slipped to seventh place with a 3-4 record but remain firmly in contention for a semifinal berth. 
 Cayuna and Alba also matched each other with 17 excellent sets apiece, although Alba edged Cayuna in scoring, 4-3.
 The victory followed another straight-sets conquest of the Capital1 Solar Spikers last weekend, further underscoring the Chameleons' consistency and growing confidence as the elimination round approaches its crucial stretch.
 While the semifinal ticket is already secured, Nxled has little reason to ease off the gas.
 The Chameleons next face powerhouse Creamline Cool Smashers on Tuesday at the SM Mall of Asia Arena, a potentially defining encounter in their bid to secure one of the coveted Top Two positions and the twice-to-beat advantage in the Final Four.
 With their offensive arsenal clicking, their defense holding firm and their composure shining through in pressure situations, the Chameleons have established themselves as a formidable contender.
 And having become the first team to reach the semis, Nxled now has another target in sight: keep the winning streak alive, finish among the Top Two and carry that same firepower, poise and winning mentality into the championship rounds.
